components.note: 心 (heart) — 悲 relates to a heavy, sorrowful heart.
非 (fēi) gives a sound distantly related to bēi, having drifted apart over time.
刂 (knife) contributes to the character's form, though its link to 剧's meaning 'drama' has faded over time.
居 (jū) gives a rhyme close to jù, with the tone shifted.
买 (to buy) — 卖 (to sell) is the flip side of buying, the other half of a transaction.
买 (mǎi) gives a sound very close to mài, differing only in tone.
Depicts a person standing with legs crossed — the crossing shape gave 交 its meaning 'to intersect, exchange, hand over.'
讠 (speech) — 谈 relates to talking, conversation
炎 (yán) gives a sound close to 谈's reading tán
弓 (bow) — the weapon being drawn.
丨 depicts the taut drawstring being pulled back — giving 引 its meaning 'to pull, draw out, attract.'
手 (hand) — 擎 (to lift, to hold up) is an act done with the hand.
敬 (jìng) gives a sound distantly related to qíng, sharing the same final but having drifted apart in initial consonant over time.
⺼ (flesh/body) — 膝 names a body part, the knee.
桼 (qī) gives a sound only distantly related to xī today, having drifted apart over time.
羊 here pictures a woven lid or cover.
皿 (dish) sits below, together giving 盖 its meaning 'lid, to cover.'
爪 (a hand/claw) — pressing down.
卩 depicts a seal or stamp — a hand pressing a seal down gave 印 its meaning 'to print, seal, stamp.'
⺮ (bamboo) — ancient texts were written on bound bamboo strips, and 第 originally referred to the sequential order of such strips, giving rise to its meaning 'ordinal number' (as in 第一, first).
宀 (a roof, house) — 安 pictures shelter.
女 (woman) — a woman safely inside a house gave 安 its meaning 'peace' or 'safety.'
讠 (speech) — 谈 relates to talking, conversation
炎 (yán) gives a sound close to 谈's reading tán
刂 (knife) — 判 originally related to cutting something apart to distinguish or decide
半 (bàn) gives a sound close to 判's reading pàn, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
矢 (arrow) — 医 originally related to treating arrow wounds, the root of its meaning 'to cure, doctor'
匸 gives a loose sound connection to 医's reading yī
冖 (a covering/roof) — represents the building or schoolhouse where learning happens.
子 (child) — 学 depicts children gathered to study.
⺍ is a small graphic element at the top of the character; its original pictorial meaning, if any, has been lost over time.
A short stroke placed below a longer one — the mirror image of 上 (up), together forming a simple, opposite pair.
日 depicts the sun as a circle with a dot or short stroke inside — a simplified picture of the sun's disc, later squared off in the standard script.
讠 (speech/writing) — the act of putting words down.
己 (oneself, private) — writing down one's own private notes or memories, giving 记 its meaning 'to record, remember.'
阝 (mound, related to walls) — 隔 describes something separated by a barrier.
鬲 (gé) is an exact match for the sound of 隔.
土 (earth) — 壁 describes a wall, often built of earth or clay.
辟 (bì) gives the sound — an exact match with 壁.
辶 (walking/movement) — relates to 运's meaning 'to move, transport,' and by extension 'fortune,' the movement of one's life.
云 (yún) gives a sound hint — 运 is pronounced yùn, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
力 (strength/force) — 动 relates to movement produced by exertion or force.
贝 (shell/money — cowrie shells were historically used as currency) — 员 originally related to counting or officials responsible for accounts, later broadening to mean 'member' or 'personnel.'
冏 (bright, a window admitting light) — appears in 商's ancient form, though its exact link to 'commerce, to discuss' is unclear today.
章 — a graphic element whose original contribution to the character's meaning has been lost over time.
人 — a lid covering the dish
良 — a dish piled with food
口 (mouth), stacked three times — many mouths talking about or judging something, the source of 品's meaning 'product, item; quality, rank.'
A picture of a nose; because people in ancient China would point to their own nose when referring to themselves, the character came to mean 'self.'
禾 (grain) — grain was one of the first things ancient people owned and kept for themselves.
厶 pictures something folded in on itself and hidden away, giving 私 its sense of 'private, personal, one's own.'
角 (horn) — 解 pictures removing a part of an animal.
牛 (ox) — together with a knife cutting between horn and ox, 解 pictures separating something into parts, giving its meaning 'to untie' or 'to explain.'
廾 (two hands) — depicts hands at work.
一 represents the latch or bar of a door; hands lifting it away gave 开 its meaning 'to open, to start.'

meanings: the seat to the right of the main guest

components.note: A short stroke placed below a longer one — the mirror image of 上 (up), together forming a simple, opposite pair.
手 is a simple picture of an open hand with the fingers spread out.

meanings: (term of endearment for a child) darling

components.note: 门 (gate, door) marks a boundary being crossed.
马 (horse) rushes through the gate — a horse charging in, giving 闯 its meaning 'to rush in, to dash.'
辶 (to walk) — 进 relates to advancing or entering, both movement-related.
井 (jǐng) gives a close sound cue — 进 is pronounced jìn, sharing similar consonant and vowel sounds.
扌 (hand) — 提 relates to lifting or carrying something by hand.
是 (shì) gives a hint of the sound — 提 is pronounced tí, a connection that has shifted over time.
高 depicts a tall tower or palace, with a roof at the top and a base below — a simple picture of height.
日 (sun) — the sun is what disappears as evening falls
免 (to escape, avoid) — pictured as the sun slipping away, giving 晚 its sense of 'late, evening'
灬 (fire) — 点 originally related to a small flame or dot of light, giving rise to the meaning 'dot' or 'point.'
占 (zhàn) gives a hint of the sound — 点 is pronounced diǎn, a connection that has drifted over the centuries.
亻 (person) plus 也 (also/additionally) — historically meant 'another person,' which developed into the third-person pronoun 'he/him.'
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.
氵 (water) — sand forms as water erodes rock over time.
少 (shǎo) shares the initial sh- with shā, though the vowel has since shifted.
Water — an unusual link, since deserts lack water.
Gives the sound mò, matching the character's reading.
文 depicts a chest marked with crossing lines, once tattoos or patterns on the body — decoration and pattern gave rise to the idea of 'writing' and 'culture.'
手 is a simple picture of an open hand with the fingers spread out.
大 (big, a person with arms and legs spread) pictures a person.
镸 (long) pictures a long piece of cloth wrapped around them, giving 套 its meaning 'cover, case.'
亻 (person) — 偶 originally described a wooden figure or idol shaped like a person, later extending to 'a pair' and 'by chance.'
禺 (yú) gives a sound distantly related to 偶's reading ǒu, having drifted apart over time.
禾 (grain/rice plant) — 种 relates to seeds and planting crops.
中 (zhōng) gives the sound — 种 is pronounced zhǒng, matching aside from tone.
方 (a flag/banner) — a shared banner under which a group gathers.
矢 (arrow) — warriors bound by oath under one flag gave 族 its meaning 'clan, ethnic group, tribe.'
⺈ (a person, bent over) — the figure whose outward expression is being depicted.
巴 — traditionally linked to desire or emotion, so together the character points to a person's expression or complexion, extended to 色's meaning 'color, appearance.'
忄 (heart) — 情 relates to feelings and emotions.
青 (qīng) gives the sound — 情 is pronounced qíng, a close match differing only in tone.
面 was originally a pictograph of a human face, with an outline around an eye — later broadening to mean 'face, surface, side.'
⺮ (bamboo) — 等 pictures bamboo strips, once used as writing tablets, being sorted.
寺 (originally a government office, later 'temple') — sorting and arranging bamboo documents at an official court gave 等 its meanings 'to wait,' 'rank,' and 'etc.'
走 (to walk, to run) — 赶 relates to pursuing or hurrying, both forms of movement.
干 (gān) gives a rhyme close to gǎn, with the tone shifted.
至 (zhì, to arrive) — carries 到's core meaning, 'to reach, to arrive'
刂 (a form of 刀, dāo) gives a sound close to 到's pronunciation dào
心 was originally a pictograph of the physical shape of a human heart, and came to represent the mind, feelings, and intention as well.
入 depicts a simple wedge or arrow shape pointing inward, showing the direction of entering.
纟 (silk/thread) — 经 originally referred to the vertical warp threads in weaving.
工 (gōng) gives a related sound cue for 经 (jīng), reflecting an older, closer pronunciation link between the two.
屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'
广 depicts a simple roofed building or shelter.
巾 (cloth) — together with a grass-like element above it, suggests a woven straw or cloth mat inside the shelter, giving 席 its meaning 'mat, seat.'
讠 (speech) — 课 relates to lessons taught through spoken instruction.
果 (guǒ) gives a sound distantly related to kè, having drifted apart over time.
禾 (grain) — 程 originally named a unit for measuring grain, extended to 'process, journey, degree.'
呈 (chéng) gives the sound — 程 is also pronounced chéng, an exact match.
宀 (a house) — the setting for the scene.
子 (a child) — a child inside the house, perhaps evoking a name being nurtured, the source of 字's meaning 'character, word; courtesy name.'
母 depicts a kneeling woman with two dots marking breasts — an image emphasizing nursing and motherhood, giving 母 its meaning 'mother.'

meanings: parent or guardian of a child

components.note: 宀 (roof) — 家 is about a home, the space under a roof.
豕 (shǐ, 'pig') supplies the ancient sound for 家; keeping a pig under one's roof was also a practical sign of a household in ancient China, though the modern readings jiā and shǐ no longer rhyme.
长 (simplified from 長) depicts an elderly figure with long flowing hair and a cane — length and seniority are linked in the original picture.
千 here pictures a tongue sticking upward.
口 (mouth) sits below it — together, a tongue sticking out of a mouth, giving 舌 its meaning.
大 (big) — in 头's simplified form, this element is linked to the idea of 'high' or topmost, since the head sits at the top of the body.
氵 (water) — relates to 消's meaning 'to disappear, dissolve,' like something dissolving in water.
肖 (xiào) gives a sound hint — 消 is pronounced xiāo, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
一 (a horizontal line) depicts something laid over the fire below.
火 (fire) — covering a flame to smother it gave 灭 its meaning 'to extinguish, to go out.'
Flesh — being fat relates to the body.
Gives the sound bàn, related to pàng but drifted apart over time.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.
页 (head) — 项 originally referred to the back of the neck, near the head, later extended to mean 'item, sum'
工 (gōng) gives a loose sound connection to 项's reading xiàng
钅 (metal) marks the material — links and chains are typically made of metal.
连 (to connect) sits beside it — metal pieces connected together, giving 链 its meaning 'chain.'
阝 (a mound/place) — relates to 际's meaning 'border, between,' an edge or boundary marker.
示 (shì) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from jì.
乐 is the simplified form of 樂, which depicted a wooden 木 instrument strung with strings 幺, played with a pick 白 — music came to represent joy, giving 乐 its meaning 'happy, music.'
走 (to walk/run) — 趣 originally related to hurrying eagerly toward something, extending to 'interesting, of interest.'
取 (qǔ) gives a sound close to qù, sharing the same syllable body and differing mainly in tone.
寸 (a hand) reaching for 旦 (originally 貝, a shell used as currency) — a picture of grasping something valuable, hence 'to obtain, to get.'
口 (mouth) — 知 relates to speaking what one knows.
矢 (shǐ) gives a hint of the sound — 知 is pronounced zhī, a connection that has faded over time.
虍 depicts a tiger's head and stripes.
彐 depicts a claw or hand — placed with the tiger, the image is of bared claws, giving 虐 its meaning 'cruel, to abuse.'
彳 (a road/step) — someone arriving on the road
寺 (a court/hall) — the destination where the visitor is welcomed
面 was originally a pictograph of a human face, with an outline around an eye — later broadening to mean 'face, surface, side.'
八 (two hands) — holding something up.
目 (a container/tray) — held between the two hands, the image behind 具's meaning 'tool, utensil.'
忄 (heart/mind) — the state of mind being described.
夬 (a decisive, resolute action) — a resolute state of mind, giving 快 its meaning 'fast, quick.'
辶 (to walk/move) — 速 relates to the speed of movement
束 (shù) gives a loose sound connection to 速's reading sù
页 (head) — 预 relates to looking ahead or foreseeing beforehand
予 (yǔ) gives a sound close to 预's reading yù, differing mainly in tone
纟 (thread) — 约 originally meant 'to bind, tie up,' extending to 'to agree, arrange' and 'approximately.'

meanings: variant of 電視台|电视台[dian4 shi4 tai2]

components.note: 电 (simplified from 電) depicts a bolt of lightning — since lightning is a natural form of electricity, the character came to mean 'electricity.'
见 (to see) — relates directly to 视's meaning 'to look at, view.'
礻 (a form of 示, shì) gives the sound — 视 is also pronounced shì, an exact match.
